name: Assisted Pistol Squat
notes: Stand on one leg holding a TRX, band, door frame or post in front of you, other leg extended forward. Sit back and down as low as you can control, keeping the standing heel down and the knee tracking over the toes, then drive back up. Use the support only as much as you need — pull less as you get stronger.

name: Chest flys
notes: Stand facing away from the rings, holding them together in front of your chest with arms straight. Keeping the arms fully extended, open them out wide to the sides and let your body lean forward in one straight line, then squeeze the rings back together in front to return. The arms stay straight the whole time; walk the feet back to make it harder.

name: chin-up isometric
notes: Pull up on a bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip until your chin is over the bar, then hold that position for the set time. Keep the shoulders pulled down away from the ears, chest up and legs still. Lower slowly under control when the time is up.

name: Cosack Squat
notes: Stand with feet very wide, toes slightly out. Shift your weight to one side and sit deep into that hip while the other leg stays straight with the toes pointing up, then push back through the middle to the other side. Keep the working heel down and the chest tall; only go as deep as you can without rounding the back.

name: Deep Squat
notes: Feet about shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Sit all the way down between your heels with heels on the floor and chest up, using your elbows to gently push the knees out. Stay relaxed and breathe in the bottom; hold onto something in front of you if you can't stay balanced yet.

name: Edge Lifts
notes: Hang a weight from a lifting edge (or a hangboard edge block) and lift it just off the floor with one hand, arm straight and fingers in a half-crimp or open hand. Hold for the set time, then switch hands. Stand tall with the shoulder engaged — don't pull with the arm or lean back — and choose a load you can hold without the fingers opening.

name: Elevated push-ups
notes: Push-up with your hands on a bench, box or wall to make it easier (the higher the surface, the easier). Keep a straight line from head to heels, lower the chest to the edge with elbows at about 45°, then push back up. Lower the surface over time as you get stronger.

name: explosive Squats
notes: Squat down under control to about parallel, then drive up as fast as possible, jumping off the floor if the session calls for it. Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees tracking over the toes, and reset before the next rep. Quality over quantity — stop the set when the speed drops.

name: Front lever
notes: Hang from a bar with straight arms and pull your body up until it is horizontal, face up, with arms pushing down toward the hips. Keep the shoulders depressed, the glutes and core tight and the body in one straight line. Use a progression (tuck, advanced tuck, one leg, straddle) that you can hold with good form.

name: Hanging Knee Raises
notes: Hang from a bar with straight arms and the shoulders engaged. Bring the knees up toward the chest by curling the pelvis, not just lifting the legs, then lower slowly. Avoid swinging — pause briefly at the bottom before the next rep.

name: Inverted Row
notes: Hang under a pair of rings set at about waist height, arms straight, heels on the floor and body in one straight line. Pull your chest up between the rings by squeezing the shoulder blades together, turning the palms in as you rise, then lower under control. Walk the feet back or bend the knees to make it easier, or walk them forward to make it harder.

name: Jumps into box
notes: Stand in front of a sturdy box, swing the arms and jump up, landing softly on top with both feet and knees bent. Stand up fully on the box, then step down — don't jump down. Pick a height you clear easily; the goal is a fast, explosive take-off, not the highest box.

name: KettleBell Deadlift
notes: Stand with the kettlebell between your feet. Push the hips back with a slight knee bend and a flat back, grab the handle, then stand up by driving the hips forward until you're tall. Keep the bell close to the body and the back neutral throughout — the movement comes from the hips, not the lower back.

name: KettleBell Squat
notes: Hold a kettlebell by the horns at chest height (goblet position), feet shoulder-width and toes slightly out. Squat down between your heels keeping the chest up and the elbows inside the knees, then drive back up. Keep the heels down and the knees tracking over the toes.

name: Negative pull-ups
notes: Start at the top of a pull-up with your chin over the bar (jump or step up to get there). Lower yourself as slowly as possible, aiming for 3–5 seconds, until your arms are fully straight. Keep the shoulders engaged all the way down and step back up for the next rep rather than pulling.

name: One-Arm Inverted Row
notes: Hold one TRX handle with one hand, lean back with the arm straight and feet wide for balance, body in a straight line. Pull your chest toward the handle without letting the hips twist or sag, then lower under control. Do all reps on one side, then switch; walk the feet forward to make it harder.

name: pancake
notes: Sit with legs wide in a straddle, knees and toes pointing up. Tilt the pelvis forward and fold your chest toward the floor, leading with the belly rather than rounding the upper back. Go only as far as you can keep the legs straight; actively press the legs into the floor and lift up slightly between reps.

name: pinch lifts
notes: Pinch a pinch block (or two plates smooth-side out) with the thumb on one side and the fingers on the other, and lift it just off the floor with a straight arm. Hold for the set time, then switch hands. Stand tall with the shoulder engaged and squeeze with the whole hand — keep the thumb involved, not just the fingertips.

name: Pistol Squat
notes: Stand on one leg with the other leg straight out in front of you. Sit all the way down on the standing leg, keeping the heel on the floor, chest forward and arms reaching out for balance, then stand back up without touching down. Keep the knee tracking over the toes; use the assisted version until you control the bottom.

name: planch twist
notes: Start in a plank on straight arms, hands under the shoulders and body in a straight line. Lift the opposite arm and leg out long, then curl them in under the body until the elbow touches the knee, and extend them back out. Keep the hips level and the core tight throughout; do all reps on one side, then switch.

name: Pull Ups
notes: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip a bit wider than the shoulders. Start by pulling the shoulders down, then pull until your chin is over the bar and lower all the way down to straight arms. Avoid kicking or swinging; use a band or negatives if you can't yet do the set reps with good form.

name: Push-ups
notes: Hands a bit wider than the shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels. Lower until the chest nearly touches the floor with elbows at about 45° from the body, then push back up to straight arms. Don't let the hips sag or pike — squeeze the glutes and core throughout.

name: repeaters
notes: On a hangboard, hang for 7 seconds and rest for 3 seconds, repeating for the whole set without letting go between hangs. Use the edge and grip set for the session and keep the arms straight with the shoulders engaged. Choose a load that lets you finish every hang with good form — stop if the grip starts to open.

name: roller
notes: Kneel holding an ab wheel under your shoulders. Roll forward slowly, extending the hips and arms, as far as you can while keeping the lower back from sagging, then pull back to the start using your core. Keep the ribs down and the glutes squeezed; shorten the range if you feel it in the lower back.

name: Split Squat
notes: Stand in a long split stance, front foot flat and back heel up. Lower straight down until the back knee is just above the floor and the front thigh is about parallel, then drive up through the front foot. Keep the torso upright and the front knee tracking over the toes; do all reps on one side, then switch.

name: squat isometric
notes: Squat down to the set depth (usually thighs parallel, or sit against a wall) and hold still for the set time. Keep the heels down, the chest up and the knees pushed out over the toes. Breathe steadily throughout; don't let the hips creep up as you fatigue.

name: Trx core
notes: With your feet in the TRX straps, start in a straight-arm plank with the body in one line. Pull the knees to the chest (or pike the hips up) using the abs, then return to the plank under control. Keep the shoulders over the hands and don't let the lower back sag between reps.

name: Wrist flexion
notes: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm facing up and the wrist just past the edge, holding a light dumbbell. Let the weight roll down toward the fingertips, then curl the wrist up as high as you can. Keep the forearm still and move slowly — only the wrist moves.

name: wrist rotations
notes: Hold a light dumbbell or a hammer by one end with the forearm resting on your thigh or a bench. Slowly rotate the forearm so the palm turns from facing down to facing up and back, keeping the elbow still. Hold further from the weighted end to make it harder.
